children: Oil edges higher in Asian trade, with front-month Brent futures hovering above the psychologically important $100-a-barrel mark. Attention in oil markets will likely be centered around diplomatic developments, says FXTM's Lukman Otunuga in commentary. Iran has warned that renewed escalation in the Middle East conflict would trigger a significant response, which could push crude prices higher, says the head of market research. However, any confirmation of direct talks between the U.S. and Iran at this week's United Nations General Assembly could place selling pressure on prices by raising expectations for Middle East supply, he adds. Front-month Brent crude-oil futures rise 0.2% to $100.51 a barrel; front-month WTI is flat at $95.80 a barrel. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
